claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at elevated temperatures.
Partial substitution of Hf with Al will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Partial substitution of Hf with Al will preserve the alloy's room-temperature mechanical properties.
Partial substitution of Hf with Al will preserve mechanical properties at elevated temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
Al has a lower atomic weight than Hf.
Replacing Hf with lower-atomic-weight Al will lower the alloy's average atomic weight and thereby reduce its density.
The Al-for-Hf substitution is expected to maintain a stable single-phase solid-solution structure.
Maintaining a stable single-phase solid solution is crucial for preserving the alloy's mechanical properties.
Al can provide solid-solution strengthening in the modified alloy.
Al can stabilize the high-entropy alloy microstructure under the stated conditions.
The proposed property retention depends on keeping Al substitution below a critical threshold that would destabilize the single-phase structure.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C under mechanical loading.
A substitution series at nominal levels of 5%, 10%, and 15% should be prepared and compared with as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Density, room-temperature tensile strength, tensile strength at 1000 °C, and phase constitution by XRD should be measured.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than 5%, tensile strength decreases by more than 10% at room temperature or 1000 °C, or XRD detects secondary phases.
